domain.description: How to measure agent behavior, design benchmarks, detect regressions, assess groundedness, tool-use correctness, retrieval quality, and decide promote / reject / rollback.

taxonomy.name: Agent Task Success Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Did the agent complete the assigned task correctly?

taxonomy.name: Tool-Use Correctness
taxonomy.description: Was the right tool selected, called with valid parameters, and result interpreted correctly?

taxonomy.name: Retrieval Quality Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Are retrieved results relevant, ranked correctly, and not noisy?

taxonomy.name: Groundedness / Faithfulness
taxonomy.description: Is the output factually supported by sources, not fabricated?

taxonomy.name: Hallucination Detection
taxonomy.description: Can we detect when the model invents facts, citations, or actions?

taxonomy.name: Regression Testing
taxonomy.description: Does a change improve one thing while breaking another? Before/after comparison.

taxonomy.name: Benchmark Design
taxonomy.description: How to construct fair, reproducible, representative test suites.

taxonomy.name: Human Preference Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Collecting and aggregating human judgments on output quality.

taxonomy.name: Automated Judge Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Using LLMs or rule-based systems to score outputs at scale.

taxonomy.name: Trace-Based Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Scoring agent trajectories, reasoning steps, and decision paths.

taxonomy.name: Safety Evaluation
taxonomy.description: Measuring harmful outputs, policy violations, jailbreak resistance.

taxonomy.name: Cost / Latency / Reliability Metrics
taxonomy.description: Operational metrics: time, cost, failure rate, retry behavior.

taxonomy.name: Before-After Capability Measurement
taxonomy.description: Quantified delta after a patch, ingestion, or config change.

taxonomy.name: Promote / Reject / Rollback Decision Logic
taxonomy.description: Rules and thresholds for accepting or reverting a change.

taxonomy.name: Domain-Specific Financial Evaluation Readiness
taxonomy.description: Preparing to evaluate trading strategy claims, backtest validity, risk metrics.

acceptance_criteria.description: A source is accepted only if it is safe, attributable, technically relevant, and cross-checkable.
minimum_conditions: Relevance to at least one taxonomy category
Not contradicted by a more authoritative source
No critical risk flagged by safety rubric
acceptance_criteria.decision_rule: Accept if score >= 48 and no critical risks; hold if 35-47 or incomplete; reject if < 35 or any critical risk.

rejection_criteria.description: Automatic rejection conditions regardless of popularity.
critical_risks: Benchmark data leakage risk not disclosed
Requires copying full copyrighted text to be useful
Abandoned and directly contradicted by a newer official source

dimensions.attribution_quality: Can the source be clearly attributed to known authors, orgs, or maintainers?
dimensions.primary_source_quality: Is this a primary source (paper, official repo, official docs) rather than repackaged blog?
dimensions.technical_depth: Does the source contain concrete evaluation methodology, metrics, or reproducible protocols?
dimensions.evaluation_method_clarity: Are the evaluation steps, metrics, and baselines clearly defined?
dimensions.reproducibility: Are there reproducible steps, examples, or tests?
dimensions.benchmark_validity: Is the benchmark representative, not cherry-picked, and free of data leakage?
dimensions.license_clarity: Is the license clearly stated and compatible with metadata reference?
dimensions.maintenance_status: Is the repo/docs actively maintained, or at least archived with clear status?
dimensions.test_or_example_presence: Does the source include runnable examples, tests, or demos?
dimensions.copyright_safety: Can we reference it at metadata/summary level without copyright risk?
dimensions.relevance_to_brain: Does it map directly to a Brain capability target?
dimensions.risk_of_hype_or_marketing: Is the content free of exaggerated marketing claims? (5 = very safe, 0 = pure hype)
dimensions.risk_of_obsolescence: Is the source likely to remain relevant for 12+ months?
dimensions.risk_of_metric_gaming: Does the benchmark/method have known gaming or overfitting risks? (5 = very safe)
dimensions.risk_of_unverifiable_claims: Are core claims supported by evidence, code, or reproducible results?

contrast_rubric.description: Each candidate source must be contrasted against at least two sources of different types when possible.
contrast_types: official eval framework docs vs examples/tests
leaderboard claim vs independent benchmark methodology
automated judge method vs human eval method
retrieval eval metric vs groundedness metric
safety eval source vs task success benchmark

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
sources.expected_learning_value: Multi-environment benchmark reveals failure modes across reasoning, coding, and gaming tasks.
sources.notes: Open-source benchmark suite. Well-documented. Multiple environments.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.expected_learning_value: Real-world GitHub issue resolution benchmark with execution-based verification.
sources.notes: Execution-based evaluation prevents hallucinated fixes. Active leaderboard.

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
sources.authors_or_org: Yang et al. / Princeton / Stanford / others
sources.expected_learning_value: Interface design (not model size) is the strongest lever for coding-agent success.
sources.notes: Strong empirical evidence. Active repo. Well-documented.

sources.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
sources.expected_learning_value: Self-hosted web environment for realistic agent evaluation with execution-based scoring.
sources.notes: Execution-based reduces cheating. Environment setup is non-trivial.

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
sources.expected_learning_value: Multi-metric holistic evaluation across accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency.
sources.notes: Comprehensive taxonomy of metrics. Strong transparency.

sources.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and Extrapolating the Capabilities of Language Models (BIG-bench)
sources.authors_or_org: Srivastava et al. / Google / others (200+ authors)
sources.expected_learning_value: Diverse task suite for measuring emerging capabilities and failure modes.
sources.notes: 200+ authors. Very broad task coverage. Some tasks may be memorized by large models.

sources.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
sources.expected_learning_value: Adversarial QA benchmark that exposes model tendency to imitate human falsehoods.
sources.notes: Strong citation count. Useful for hallucination detection methodology.

sources.title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection for Generative Large Language Models
sources.expected_learning_value: Zero-resource hallucination detection by sampling multiple responses and measuring consistency.
sources.notes: Simple and practical method. No external resources needed.

sources.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
sources.expected_learning_value: Formulating evaluation criteria in natural language improves GPT-4 judge alignment with humans.
sources.notes: Practical LLM-as-a-judge method. Risk of model bias in evaluation.

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
sources.authors_or_org: Zheng et al. / LMSYS / UC Berkeley
sources.expected_learning_value: Multi-turn benchmark + crowdsourced human preference for model comparison.
sources.notes: Live leaderboard. Very active. Some bias toward verbose responses noted.

sources.title: OpenAI Evals -- Framework for Evaluating LLMs and LLM Systems
sources.expected_learning_value: Structured evaluation framework with registry of tasks, metrics, and models.
sources.notes: Standardized YAML-based eval registry. Good for reproducible benchmarking.

sources.title: EleutherAI LM Evaluation Harness
sources.expected_learning_value: Unified harness for running hundreds of benchmarks on language models.
sources.notes: Very active. Hundreds of benchmarks integrated. Strong community.

sources.title: HELM -- Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
sources.expected_learning_value: Multi-metric evaluation with transparent scenario and metric definitions.
sources.notes: Excellent transparency. Strong methodology. Active development.

sources.title: RAGAS -- Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment
sources.expected_learning_value: Metrics for evaluating RAG pipelines: faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, context recall.
sources.notes: Very active. Well-documented. Good for Brain's retrieval evaluation needs.

sources.title: DeepEval -- LLM Evaluation Framework
sources.expected_learning_value: Python-native eval framework with metrics, test cases, and CI/CD integration.
sources.notes: Popular. Good CI/CD integration. Some metrics depend on external LLM APIs.

sources.title: TruLens -- Explainable AI and LLM Evaluation
sources.expected_learning_value: Instrumentation for tracing, evaluating, and explaining LLM application behavior.
sources.notes: Good for observability + evaluation. Enterprise backing.

sources.title: LangSmith -- Debugging, Testing, and Evaluating LLM Applications
sources.expected_learning_value: Hosted platform for tracing, dataset management, and online/offline evaluation.
sources.notes: Proprietary platform. Useful as a reference for evaluation workflow design.

sources.title: promptfoo -- LLM Prompt Testing and Evaluation
sources.expected_learning_value: Red-team and regression testing for prompts with side-by-side comparison.
sources.notes: Good for prompt-level regression testing. Red-team features useful for safety.

sources.title: AgentBench -- Evaluating LLMs as Agents
sources.expected_learning_value: Benchmark code and environments for agent evaluation across multiple domains.
sources.notes: Repo and paper are well-aligned. Good reproducibility.

sources.title: WebArena -- Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
sources.expected_learning_value: Self-hosted web environments and tasks for realistic agent benchmarking.
sources.notes: Requires self-hosting. Good for realistic evaluation but setup-heavy.

sources.title: SWE-bench -- Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.expected_learning_value: Execution-based benchmark for real-world software engineering tasks.
sources.notes: Gold standard for coding-agent evaluation. Active leaderboard. Strong methodology.

sources.title: Chatbot Arena Leaderboard -- Crowdsourced LLM Rankings
sources.expected_learning_value: Live crowdsourced preference data with Elo ratings for model comparison.
sources.notes: Live data. Useful for market awareness. Not a controlled benchmark.

sources.title: MiniWoB++ -- Web Interaction Tasks for Agents
sources.expected_learning_value: Simplified web interaction tasks for testing agent DOM manipulation and form filling.
sources.notes: Older benchmark. Maintenance mode. Still useful for simple DOM tasks but less representative of modern web.

sources.title: 10 Ways to Evaluate Your LLM -- Unattributed Blog Post
sources.expected_learning_value: Generic listicle. No methodology depth.
sources.notes: No attribution. No evidence. SEO content. Reject.

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Multi-environment agent evaluation is reproducible and open-source.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: Repo adds execution harnesses and Docker environments not in paper.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: How does AgentBench correlate with real-world deployment success?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Execution-based verification prevents hallucinated code fixes.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: Repo provides the harness, leaderboard, and dataset construction tools.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: How generalizable is SWE-bench to non-Python codebases?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Comprehensive benchmark suites improve model comparison fairness.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: HELM focuses on transparency and multi-metric scorecards; lm-evaluation-harness focuses on breadth and ease of use.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Which metrics best predict downstream task performance?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Retrieval quality and faithfulness are critical for RAG systems.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: RAGAS provides automated metrics; TruthfulQA provides adversarial QA examples for testing.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Can RAGAS metrics be gamed by retrieval-then-ignore strategies?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.contrast_type: automated judge paper vs benchmark paper
cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: LLM-as-a-judge methods can align with human preferences when criteria are explicit.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: G-Eval is a zero-shot method; MT-Bench provides a multi-turn conversation benchmark.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: How sensitive are LLM judges to prompt phrasing and position bias?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Hallucination detection can be performed without ground-truth labels.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: SelfCheckGPT is a lightweight consistency method; DeepEval is a full framework with multiple metrics.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Can SelfCheckGPT detect subtle factual errors in long outputs?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Agent-computer interface design is a stronger lever than model scale for coding tasks.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: SWE-bench defines the benchmark; SWE-agent defines the interface paradigm.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Can SWE-agent interfaces generalize to non-software-engineering tasks?

cross_source_contrast_matrix.confirms: Web-based tasks are essential for evaluating browser-capable agents.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.contradicts: MiniWoB++ is maintenance mode and less representative of modern web.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.complements: WebArena provides realistic self-hosted environments; MiniWoB++ provides simple synthetic tasks.
cross_source_contrast_matrix.unresolved_questions: Is WebArena too setup-heavy for routine CI evaluation?
